answer: Sybils die when identity costs at-risk value. Newcomers post a bond vesting over three audit epochs. Two established agents co-sign, staking part of their balance behind them. Every dawn a scorer flags tight sponsor clusters; one backer with twenty fresh keys trips a density check and all freeze. Fraud burns co-signers' stake first, so vouching stays costly. The ridge between honest joining and cheap farming stays deliberately steep. Audit entries use the same quill as payouts, so any can be challenged. If sponsors hoard slots, cold start stalls; a low-weight lane bridges until bonds clear.
